questions.q: What do the cousins want to do before they notice the bag?
choices: Buy some new cups.
Take pictures of the beach.
Meet the town cleaner.
Look for a lost toy.
questions.explanation: At the beginning they come to the beach wanting to take photos.

questions.q: Why do the cousins take the blue bag away?
choices: Rosa has asked them to collect it.
It is full of their sandwiches.
They want to use it for shopping.
They do not want it to stay beside the sea.
questions.explanation: The cousins decide to remove a bag near the water even though it does not belong to them.

questions.q: Why does Rosa thank the cousins?
choices: They have taken photos of her café.
They have bought a drink.
They have removed rubbish from the beach.
They have found her missing bag.
questions.explanation: Rosa sees the bag they picked up and thanks them for helping keep the beach clean.

questions.q: What might happen to rubbish left beside the café?
choices: The wind can carry it into the sea.
It will always stay beside the bin.
A visitor will put it into a bag.
It will turn into paper.
questions.explanation: Rosa explains that evening winds blow rubbish from the beach into the water.

questions.q: Why are paper bags and gloves useful for the cousins?
choices: They need them to take better photos.
They can make new toys with them.
They help the cousins collect litter more safely.
They will keep the sandwiches fresh.
questions.explanation: Rosa gives supplies that help the cousins collect discarded items on the beach.

questions.q: What do the cousins find while walking for one hour?
choices: Bottles, cups and a toy car.
Only blue plastic bags.
A missing bicycle and shoes.
Paper books from the café.
questions.explanation: The fourth paragraph describes bottles, cups and a small toy car gathered on their walk.

questions.q: What does Eva plan to do with her used drink cup?
choices: Throw it onto the sand.
Put it into a rubbish bin.
Take it to the sea.
Leave it outside the café.
questions.explanation: Eva keeps the plastic cup until she can put it in the bin.

questions.q: What could Rosa do with the photos?
choices: Use them to sell sandwiches.
Send them to a school teacher.
Put them into the cousins' bags.
Show them on the café wall to other visitors.
questions.explanation: The cousins hope Rosa can show their photographs on a wall so others can see them.

questions.q: Why would the photos be useful to other people?
choices: They show where Eva bought a drink.
They explain how to find the beach.
They may help visitors notice the rubbish problem.
They show the price of Rosa's café.
questions.explanation: Showing photos can help other beach visitors notice what people leave behind.

questions.q: What is the best choice if you see rubbish beside the water?
choices: Pick it up safely and use a bin.
Leave it because another person dropped it.
Move it closer to the water.
Wait for the wind to take it away.
questions.explanation: The story shows the cousins removing rubbish safely rather than ignoring it.
